display: Second-year nursing student in Toronto, international from Cebu. I work night shifts, sing soprano in a Filipino church choir and love K-dramas.

signals.text: Winter's not even here and I'm already tired. Night shifts plus full-time nursing classes are wearing me down.
I'm looking for a warm, affordable winter coat. The only jacket I own is a cotton one from Cebu.
I miss home and my lola. I'd love more Filipino and Cebuano community around me in Toronto.
My clinical placement starts in January and I'd like advice from nurses on how to prepare.
I need help with pharmacology, like ACE inhibitors vs ARBs and drug classes in general. My final is October 20.
My pharmacology midterm came back at 52%. I know the material but I was too tired in the exam, and I need at least 65% on the final to pass.
I study on the bus and in the break room, so I only get short, scattered blocks of study time.
My manager asked me to take two more shifts. I felt bad saying no and bad saying yes, and I don't know how to protect my study time.
I have CAD 90 saved toward a coat, but the one I saw costs $149. I'm waiting for a sale or a secondhand option.
Choir needs me on Sundays and I want to keep going, but I'm stretched thin.
I'm skipping lunch and eating half a sandwich on my break to make the money stretch. Cheap, filling meals or groceries would really help.
I send money home to Cebu every month for family needs and school fees, so my budget is tight and fixed.
I tell my family I'm fine and eating well. I don't want them to worry, so I carry the stress alone.

offers.text: I'm fluent in English, Cebuano and Tagalog. I can help newcomers or Filipino families with translation, interpreting or just conversation.
I'm a soprano and can sing at Filipino community events, masses, weddings or Christmas programs. I know church-choir repertoire like Ave Maria.
I'm a second-year nursing student and can share what the first two years of a Canadian nursing program are really like. I can give advice on balancing school with a night job.
I'm pallet-jack certified with night stocking and warehouse experience. I can advise on stock-room routines and safe lifting.
I have a budget spreadsheet and can share the template with other students who are tight on money. I can also share how I get around Toronto on a bus pass.
I can be a study partner or note-swapper for nursing fundamentals and other early nursing courses. I'll trade for pharmacology help.
I can introduce people to Toronto's Filipino church-choir community, where people like Auntie Gloria look after newcomers.
I can give honest K-drama recommendations and keep someone company with a long subway-ride chat.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a nurse educator and I tutor nursing students in pharmacology for free or at low cost. Are you struggling with cardiovascular drug classes before a final?
catchers.can: I'd take short remote or after-class sessions for ACE inhibitors vs ARBs and other drug classes. They'd have to fit around my night shifts, and I can pay little or nothing.
catchers.confirm: Is the tutoring free or very low cost, and can it be done in short remote sessions outside overnight hours?

catchers.hypo: I have a warm winter coat I no longer wear, rated for Toronto winters. I'd like it to go to a student who needs it.
catchers.can: I could take it and put it to use right away. I'd happily pay a small amount or return the favour by singing at an event.
catchers.confirm: Is it a real winter coat, warm enough for temperatures below -15°C, and not just a fashion jacket?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Filipino who just moved to Toronto and I miss home. Is there a church or choir community I could join?
catchers.can: I can invite them to my Filipino church choir and introduce them to Auntie Gloria and the community. People there often bring food and look after newcomers.
catchers.confirm: Does this person speak Filipino, Tagalog or Cebuano and live in the Toronto area?

catchers.hypo: Our community group runs a scholarship fund for high-school students in Cebu who can't pay tuition. Do you know any families who need it?
catchers.can: I can pass the details to my family in Cebu, where a Grade 10 student needs help with school fees. I'd take it from there.
catchers.confirm: Does it cover Grade 10 students in Cebu, and is it a grant with no repayment?

catchers.hypo: I'm a registered nurse in Ontario and I like mentoring students before their first clinical placement. What would you like to know?
catchers.can: I'd ask about preparing for my January placement, including what to bring, how to handle shifts and how to ask for feedback.
catchers.confirm: Have you worked as a nurse in an Ontario hospital or clinic in the last five years?

catchers.hypo: Our church needs a soprano for the Christmas season, with rehearsals on weekends and some Filipino-language songs.
catchers.can: I can sing, and I can bring my choir group along if there's room. I'd have to keep Sundays for my own church.
catchers.confirm: Are the rehearsals and performances on weekends or daytime, not overnight, and are Filipino songs welcome?

catchers.hypo: Our community fridge or student food program hands out free groceries and meals to students. Does anyone you know need it?
catchers.can: I'd come by after my shift, and I can tell other students about it. I can volunteer a little in return when my schedule allows.
catchers.confirm: Is it free, open to students with just a student ID, and open on days or hours that suit a night-shift worker?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nursing student in Toronto with a pharmacology final on October 20. Do you want to swap notes and quiz each other?
catchers.can: I'd join a study group or swap flashcards. I'd offer my notes on nursing fundamentals in return and keep sessions short.
catchers.confirm: Are you currently taking pharmacology with a final coming up in October?

catchers.hypo: A local clinic needs a volunteer Cebuano or Tagalog speaker to help patients a few hours a month. Do you know someone?
catchers.can: I can help with interpreting and with explaining things to patients, and it would be good nursing experience. Hours would have to stay small.
catchers.confirm: Is it a small commitment of about three hours a week or less, with schedules that can flex around classes?

forbids.text: Sundays are reserved for church, choir and my video call with Lola.
I can't take on overnight commitments, because I already work night shifts.
I can't take on any new big commitments before my pharmacology final on October 20.
I can't pay for tutoring or courses, because my budget is tight and fixed.
I won't work extra hours that cut into study and sleep time.

projects.name: Pharmacology final recovery
projects.text: I'm aiming to pass my pharmacology final on October 20 after a 52% midterm. I need short, regular study help that fits around night shifts.
roles_needed: someone to quiz me by phone or video

projects.name: Winter coat fund
projects.text: I'm saving for a proper winter coat for Toronto and have part of the money. I'd consider a good secondhand coat.
roles_needed: tip on sales or student discounts

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share my work schedule and my pharmacology midterm result, so a tutor or helper can see what I need.
policy.t2: Once I trust the other person and know who they are, I'll share that I send money home and sometimes skip meals, so they can offer real help.
policy.never: Visa, immigration or study-permit details, and my family's medical records or conditions.
